It's not bad. You did an amazing job with the hands and face, but the body looks a bit flat. Think about what is under the fabric when you draw clothes. If I can offer some suggestions:

The band around her waist should not be so flat. It would be relatively straight across her belly, then curve up only around her sides where her torso starts to curve around to her back.

The collar of the dress should also not be so straight. It would curve as it goes over her clavicle and her traps.

The folds in her dress also don't really make any sense. The skirt looks amazing. You did a good job curving the folds inward as they go under the band, but then there are no folds at the top. If the top of her dress is intended to be loose it would have a few, smaller folds around the band where the fabric is gathered. If the top is meant to be tight, then the curves of her torso need to be more defined. You did a wonderful job with the curves and shape of the arms, especially the right arm, so it's clear that you don't have issues with drawing people too angularly. You just need to consider how those curve will affect the fabric over them.

The fabric also needs some thickness to it. The collar would be slightly higher than the rest of her dress because it's sitting on top of the blue fabric. The same applies to the band; it should stick out slightly further than the blue portion of the dress.

To really shown the contours of what's under the fabric, you might also consider foreshortening the design on the fabric. E.g. the flowers on the sides of the dress would not look the same as the flowers at the front. You're looking at the flowers in the front of the dress head-on, so the flower would not be distorted, but as the fabric turns, the pattern would turn with it, and the flowers would look thinner.
